title: Workload Mixer SLA Emulator and Customer Onboarding Kit
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Deliver a repeatable workload-mixer harness and an associated acceptance playbook for onboarding Dedicated capacity customers. The mixer generates multi-tenant realistic blends (chat, single-turn generation, embeddings) with configurable burstiness, KV/prefix cache state, and autoscaler policy knobs so SRE/Product can validate throughput guarantees and revenue-grade SLAs before signoff.
background: Customers expect predictable throughput and tail latency from Dedicated. Current load tests are either synthetic (single-pattern) or full replay which can be noisy and hard to parameterize. We need a controllable emulator that can model mixed workloads, autoscaler behavior, and cache warmup convergence to provide deterministic acceptance runs and reproducible artifacts for customer signoff.
goals: Provide a harness that can synthesize multi-tenant request mixes with configurable distributions and deterministic seeds
Expose autoscaler policy knobs (min/max pools, target_util, scale-up/down cooldowns) and observe their effect on SLA attainment
Create a customer acceptance checklist and a runnable playbook to validate throughput guarantees and rollout readiness
Produce standardized artifacts (graphs, traces, CSVs) and a PR template for Dedicated customer signoff
success_metrics: Acceptance playbook reduces customer signoff time from average 5 days to <=24 hours
Harness reproducibility: same seed + policy yields latency curves within 5% across runs
Automated run artifacts include p50/p95/p99/p999 latencies, GPU utilization, tokens/sec, queue depth, and cost estimate per 1M tokens
At least two pilot customers complete the onboarding kit during the release window
scope: Design and implement the Workload Mixer (generator + orchestrator)
Integrate harness output with our metrics pipeline (Prometheus exporters and perf dashboards)
Author the customer acceptance playbook and a runnable CLI to execute the standard scenario
Provide post-run artifact packaging (S3/Drive link) and PR checklist for sales/solutions
out_of_scope: Full-e2e billing reconciliation (we will provide cost estimates but not final billing workflows)
Large-scale cluster autoscaler rewrite — we only simulate policy impacts and produce test data
Creating new GPU kernels or model-level performance optimizations
deliverables: standard scenario YAMLs (steady, burst, long-tail, cold-cache)
customer-acceptance-playbook.md with checklist and run commands
Grafana dashboard template and Prometheus scrape configs
Automated artifact packager that uploads run outputs to artifacts.redwood.ai/<customer>-<run>
approach: Phase 1: Prototype generator that supports Poisson, bursty Pareto, and scheduled spike distributions; integrate with a lightweight runner to hit the runtime HTTP API
Phase 2: Add KV/prefix cache modeling (warm/cold states) and deterministic seed to control cache hits during run
Phase 3: Autoscaler emulator that applies policy knobs and simulates scale decisions (with optional dry-run vs real-scale modes)
Phase 4: Standardize scenario library and acceptance checklist; run two internal pilots and iterate
Phase 5: Publish images, docs, and onboarding checklist; provide handover to Solutions + SRE
harness_components: generator: workload-mixer (Go) with pluggable distribution engines
orchestrator: run-controller that coordinates stages (ramp, steady, spike, cooldown)
recorder: lightweight trace collector that captures request/response metadata and token counts
exporter: Prometheus client + Grafana dashboards for pX latency, GPU util, queue depth
artifact-packager: zips logs/metrics, uploads to artifacts bucket, signs run manifest
benchmarking_methodology: 1) Select representative request traces from anonymized customer logs and create a small 'seed set' of templates
2) Convert traces into parametric templates with variable prompt lengths and response token distributions
3) Run four canonical scenarios: cold-cache steady-state, warmed-cache steady-state, burst spike (3x baseline for 10m), long-tail churn (many small requests + occasional large ones)
4) For each scenario, sweep autoscaler policies (min/max/target/scale cooldown) and record outcomes using deterministic seeds
5) Collect p50/p95/p99/p999 latency, tokens/sec, model throughput, GPU utilization, queue_depth histogram, and error rates across runs
6) Produce a cost-estimate model using per-GPU hour and token accounting to provide an expected dollars-per-1M-tokens number
test_plan: Unit tests for distribution samplers and seed reproducibility
Integration test: mixer -> runtime through local dev stack with mock model to verify request shapes
Staging e2e: run full canonical scenarios against a small Dedicated cluster and record artifacts
Recovery tests: simulate node OOM/crash and network delay to assert graceful fallback and autoscaler response
Acceptance run: joint session with Solutions + Customer (if available) running standard scenario and checklist
acceptance_criteria: Playbook run completes without unhandled runtime errors and artifacts are produced
For the warmed-cache steady-state scenario, the cluster maintains expected throughput within 10% of observed baseline for 30m
p95 latency under the customer SLA for the run profile and p999 within the 'graceful degradation' envelope defined in the playbook
Autoscaler policy sweeps produce repeatable scale events and documented decision boundaries
Customer acceptance checklist items are signed by Solutions and SRE and attached to the run artifact
rollout_plan: Internal pilot with SRE and 2 pilot customers during release window
Bake period: 3 days of continuous runs on a Dedicated shard to validate stability
Publish public docs and customer onboarding kit in Confluence and internal Drive
Train Solutions engineers with a 60-minute walkthrough and a drill where they run the acceptance playbook
Mark feature GA for Dedicated sales once two customers complete the kit and defects are triaged
risks: Determinism: external dependencies (time, jitter) could make runs non-reproducible if we don't strictly control seeding
Scale: running large canonical scenarios is resource-heavy and may interfere with other staging activity
Customer expectations: playbook must make clear that empirical runs are representative but not absolute guarantees for all workloads
Complexity of autoscaler emulation could diverge from production autoscaler behaviors if policy logic changes
open_questions: Do we run the autoscaler emulator in 'dry-run' only, or attempt real scaling in pilot clusters?
What is the canonical per-GPU cost used for the cost-estimate model (finance to confirm)?
Should the mixer support function-calls / tool-calling request shapes or only standard completion/chat endpoints?
Who is the owner for the artifact storage retention policy (SRE or Solutions)?
